app.title: Ichimon
newGame.lead: A retired wrestler, you opened your own stable today. Raise your disciples and leave an heir before you retire at 65.
newGame.style.yotsu: Grab the belt and drive out
newGame.note: Money, rankings and elder-name rules follow real sumo (some values estimated). Wrestler and stable names are fictional.
action.hint: When you are ready, go to the tournament.
action.hintRetire: A disciple wants to retire. If you continue without answering, the retirement is accepted.
quit.title: Close the stable?
quit.body: This stable's records will be erased.
retire.title: Retirement request
candidates.title: Applicants
candidates.note: Accepted recruits do maezumo next tournament and appear on the banzuke after that. The stars are your own guess and can be wrong.
stable.title: Disciples ({count} / {cap})
policy.label: Training
basho.label: Year {year}, {name}
banzuke.note: ◆ marks your wrestlers. Records are from last tournament.
ledger.title: Ledger (last 2 months)
ledger.note: Association payments use reported real amounts. Expenses and supporters are estimates. Stable deficits come out of the master's savings; when those run out, the stable closes.
lineage.title: Masters of the line
lineage.successorNote: At 65 you choose a successor from the stable's elders. To become an elder a wrestler needs the qualification (1 tournament in sanyaku, 20 in makuuchi or 30 as sekitori, and Japanese nationality) and a free elder name. Free names now: {free}
lineage.kakunEmpty: None yet. One is added at each succession.
kakun.tachiai.name: Hit hard at the charge
kakun.yotsuFirst.name: Never let go of the belt
kakun.craft.name: Use the whole ring
kakun.chanko.name: Finish your chanko
kakun.chanko.desc: Bulk-up gains more weight. Food costs +10%
kakun.restDay.name: Rest is training too
kakun.thrift.name: Turn off the lights
kakun.title: Add a house rule
kakun.body: The first job of generation {generation}: keep one lesson from the previous era.
kakun.replace: The board is full. Replace which one?
report.title: Results: {basho}
report.noneMine: None of your disciples are on the banzuke.
report.retiredOyakata: {name} retires and stays on as an elder.
successor.title: Retirement age
successor.body: Master {name} is {age} and must retire. Choose who inherits the stable.
independence.title: Request to go independent
independence.body: Master {name} (formerly {shikona}, age {age}) wants a stable of his own.
independence.note: If you agree, he opens a branch stable in your ichimon. Branch promotions add to your prestige, and a branch can carry on the line if the main stable has no successor. He may take up to {max} disciples. Continuing without answering means you asked him to stay.
takeOver.title: No successor
takeOver.body: Master {name} is {age} and must retire, but no elder can inherit. You can close the main stable and take over a branch (your disciples move there).
family.title: Family tree
family.note: Under each master are the elders who came from his stable. Branch stables run on their own; their sekitori add to your prestige.
facility.title: Facilities and contracts
facility.note: Buildings are paid once from the stable account and have upkeep. Contracts are paid every tournament and can be changed any time. All amounts are estimates. Current cost per tournament: {upkeep}
facility.dorm.name: Dormitory
facility.dojo.name: Practice ring
facility.dojo.desc: New ring, posts and equipment. Training grows 6% more per level
facility.trainer.name: Trainer and clinic
facility.trainer.desc: 20% fewer injuries per level, faster recovery
facility.scout.name: Scouting network
facility.scout.desc: Ties with schools and local clubs. More applicants and more accurate reads
bout.title: {day} bout
report.hoshitoriNote: ○ win ● loss ■ absent. Tap a mark to watch the bout.
jungyo.spring: Spring tour: sekitori travel the regions. A little tiring, but popularity grows.
jungyo.summer: Summer tour: sekitori travel the regions. The heat is tiring, but popularity grows.
jungyo.autumn: Autumn tour: sekitori travel the regions. A little tiring, but popularity grows.
jungyo.winter: Winter tour: sekitori travel the regions. A little tiring, but popularity grows.
newGame.artAria: The master in front of the stable curtain, a disciple stamping and a new recruit sliding
report.playoff: The makuuchi title went to a playoff ({names}).
hurt.label: Next tournament
hurt.note: Injured. Resting heals him but he sits out and drops in the rankings (there is no injury exemption). Playing protects his rank, but he is weaker and the injury may not heal or may get worse.
detail.honorsValue: Makuuchi titles {yusho}, other division titles {other}, Outstanding {shukun}, Fighting Spirit {kanto}, Technique {gino}, kinboshi {kinboshi}
detail.moneyValue: Received so far {earned} (salary, bonuses, prize banners, prizes), mochikyukin ¥{mochikyukin}
detail.toshiyoriOk: Qualified (can become an elder on retirement, if a name is free)
detail.toshiyoriLeft: To qualify: {sanyaku} more in sanyaku, {makuuchi} more in makuuchi or {sekitori} more as sekitori (any one)
detail.chartNote: Higher is better. Filled dot: winning record, hollow: losing, large: title. Hover a dot for rank and record.
detail.noTrack: No records yet (recorded while in your stable).
alumni.title: Former wrestlers ({count})
happening.supporterParty.title: Supporters' gathering
happening.supporterParty.body: The head of the supporters' club called: "Do bring the sekitori to the next gathering."
happening.supporterParty.withSekitori.de: Bigger gifts and more prestige. The sekitori get a little tired
happening.supporterParty.masterOnly.desc: Smaller gifts. The disciples keep training
happening.supporterParty.decline.desc: Nothing happens (the chairman looks a little lonely)
happening.demegeiko.title: Training invitation
happening.demegeiko.body: A strong stable invites your wrestlers to train at their ring.
happening.demegeiko.send.desc: Next training grows more. Tiring, with a small injury risk
happening.tvInterview.title: TV feature
happening.tvInterview.body: The evening news wants to follow a sekitori through his day.
happening.tvInterview.accept.desc: Prestige rises. The sekitori get a little tired
happening.kidsSumo.title: Kids' sumo
happening.kidsSumo.body: The local children's tournament asks to borrow your ring and have your disciples coach.
happening.kidsSumo.help.desc: Prestige rises. Some money for chanko, and the disciples get a little tired
happening.famousDoctor.title: A good doctor
happening.famousDoctor.body: A supporter offers to introduce a skilled orthopedist for the injured {name}.
happening.famousDoctor.treat.desc: The injury heals one tournament sooner
happening.promisingKid.title: A promising boy
happening.promisingKid.body: A local sumo contact says there is an amazing junior high student.
happening.promisingKid.visit.desc: A highly talented applicant joins the list (you still decide whether to accept)
happening.riceGift.title: Gift from rice country
happening.riceGift.body: A supporter from rice country sent a mountain of rice and vegetables.
happening.riceGift.thank.desc: Saves on food and adds a little prestige
happening.riceGift.receive.desc: Saves a little more on food
share.saveTree: Save the family tree as an image
share.failed: Could not make the image. Please try again.
assoc.title: Sumo Association (fictional)
assoc.note: Every stable belongs to one of five ichimon. When a master retires, a coach swaps elder names with him and inherits the stable; with no heir the stable closes and its wrestlers move within the ichimon. There are 105 elder names, and one must be free to become an elder.
assoc.noFree: No elder names are free right now.
journal.title: Stable journal
journal.note: Events of your stable and its branches. Names are as they were at the time.
journal.retire.oyakata: Takes the elder name {name} and stays as a coach.
journal.retire.stays: Stays in the Association as an elder.
journal.independence: Elder {stable} (former {shikona}) goes independent and opens {stable} stable.
journal.successor: Generation {generation}: elder {stable} (former {shikona}) takes over the stable.
journal.branchSucceeded: Former {shikona} takes over the branch {stable} stable.
journal.earlier: Smaller events before this point were not recorded.
save.title: Save file
save.note: Export a file to continue on another device or browser.
save.importError: This file could not be read (not an Ichimon save, or damaged).
save.importConfirm: Load {stable} stable (generation {generation}, year {year}). Your current stable will be replaced.
bout.tachiai.harizashi: {a} slaps and gets an inside grip.
bout.tachiai.migiyotsu: They lock up, right hand inside.
bout.tachiai.hidariyotsu: They lock up, left hand inside.
bout.beat.pressInEdge: {a} drives on. {b} is at the straw!
bout.beat.stall: They stall in the middle, both breathing hard.
happening.tanimachiDinner.title: Dinner with a patron
happening.tanimachiDinner.body: A longtime patron would like a quiet dinner with {name}.
happening.tanimachiDinner.go.desc: A little prestige. A little heavier and a little tired.
happening.tanimachiDinner.master.desc: You pay for a gift. A little prestige.
happening.newSponsor.title: A new sponsor
happening.newSponsor.body: The president of a local construction firm wants to join the supporters’ club.
happening.newSponsor.askMore.desc: ¥2M if it works. Nothing if not.
happening.sponsorScandal.title: Trouble at a sponsor
happening.sponsorScandal.body: A weekly magazine is reporting on a sponsor executive’s company. The stable is named in it.
happening.sponsorScandal.cutTies.desc: Lose ¥800k of support. Gain prestige for doing the right thing.
happening.sponsorScandal.stayQuiet.desc: It may blow over. If it doesn’t, prestige drops a lot.
happening.sponsorScandal.stayQuiet.hit: A follow-up story named the stable prominently.
happening.hometownCheer.title: Hometown supporters
happening.hometownCheer.body: {name}’s hometown wants to hold a cheering party.
happening.hometownCheer.go.desc: Gifts come in and {name} trains harder. A little tired.
happening.kenshoOffer.title: A sponsor banner
happening.kenshoOffer.body: A company wants to put prize banners on your sekitori’s bouts.
happening.merchandise.title: Stable merchandise
happening.merchandise.body: A vendor proposes making towels and teacups with your sekitori’s name.
happening.merchandise.make.desc: Returns ¥1.8M if it sells. It may not.
happening.merchandise.make.hit: The towels sold out during the tournament.
happening.merchandise.make.miss: Boxes of teacups are piling up.
happening.chankoVideo.title: Chanko video
happening.chankoVideo.body: A young wrestler wants to stream the stable’s chanko on video.
happening.chankoVideo.film.desc: A little prestige, a little fatigue. A hit brings ad money and more prestige.
happening.chankoVideo.film.hit: The views took off and ad money came in.
happening.rengoKeiko.title: Ichimon joint practice
happening.rengoKeiko.body: The ichimon is holding a joint practice day.
happening.rengoKeiko.attend.desc: Better training and some prestige. A little tired.
happening.soken.title: Open practice
happening.soken.body: Before the tournament there is an open practice in front of the Yokozuna Deliberation Council.
happening.soken.attend.desc: Tense training pays off. A little prestige and fatigue.
happening.kneeWorry.title: A sore knee
happening.kneeWorry.body: After practice, {name} keeps rubbing a knee.
happening.kneeWorry.rest.desc: Fatigue drops a lot, but the next training gains less.
happening.kneeWorry.pushOn.desc: Better gains, but there’s a risk of injury.
happening.guestCoach.title: A former yokozuna visits
happening.guestCoach.body: A retired yokozuna offers to come and coach for a few days.
happening.guestCoach.accept.desc: Everyone trains better next time. A little tired.
happening.bulkUp.title: Bulking up
happening.bulkUp.body: {name} says he wants to get bigger.
happening.bulkUp.eat.desc: +5 kg. A little extra food cost.
happening.bulkUp.balanced.desc: +2 kg and a small gain in his best skill.
happening.lateStudy.title: Late-night study
happening.lateStudy.body: {name} stays up late studying bout videos.
happening.strictSenior.title: A strict senior
happening.strictSenior.body: A senior wrestler drills {name} hard every morning.
happening.strictSenior.leave.desc: Strong gains. He might want to quit.
happening.summerCamp.title: Summer camp
happening.summerCamp.body: A town in the countryside offers to host a summer training camp.
happening.summerCamp.go.desc: Big training gains for everyone. Tiring. Some prestige.
happening.heatWave.title: Heat wave
happening.heatWave.body: The thermometer in the practice room passed 35°C.
happening.coldSnap.title: A cold snap
happening.coldSnap.body: The practice room is freezing in the morning.
happening.homesick.title: Homesick
happening.homesick.body: The new recruit {name} seems to be crying at night.
happening.homesick.homeVisit: Send him home for a few days
happening.runaway.title: Run away
happening.runaway.body: In the morning, {name}’s futon is empty and some things are gone.
happening.runaway.fetch.desc: Travel costs. He usually comes back.
happening.parentsVisit.title: Parents visit
happening.parentsVisit.body: {name}’s parents want to watch practice before the tournament.
happening.newChanko.title: New chanko
happening.newChanko.body: {name}, on chanko duty, came up with a new recipe.
happening.newChanko.praise.desc: Everyone gains a little weight. Slightly higher food cost.
happening.snsTrouble.title: Social media flap
happening.snsTrouble.body: A photo {name} posted is drawing unwanted attention.
happening.snsTrouble.apologize.desc: A little prestige lost, but it ends there.
happening.snsTrouble.phoneBan.desc: A little prestige lost. Grumbling wears everyone out.
happening.snsTrouble.ignore.desc: It may die down. If it spreads, prestige drops a lot.
happening.snsTrouble.ignore.hit: A daytime TV show picked it up.
happening.snsTrouble.ignore.miss: By the next day no one remembered.
happening.drinkingTrouble.title: Trouble at a bar
happening.drinkingTrouble.body: A bar called: {name} caused a scene last night.
happening.drinkingTrouble.punish.desc: Less training next time. A little prestige for taking it seriously.
happening.drinkingTrouble.protect.desc: Nothing if it stays quiet. A big prestige loss if it gets out.
happening.drinkingTrouble.protect.hit: It ended up in a weekly magazine.
happening.wedding.title: Wedding news
happening.wedding.body: {name} came to say there is someone he wants to marry. As a sekitori, he may marry and live outside the stable.
happening.wedding.celebrate.desc: A gift from your savings. Prestige rises and {name} is spurred on. He will live outside the stable
happening.wedding.quiet.desc: {name} is a little spurred on. He will live outside the stable
happening.japaneseClass.title: Japanese lessons
happening.japaneseClass.school.desc: He settles in and trains a bit better.
happening.japaneseClass.self: He can learn at the stable
happening.alumniVisit.title: A former wrestler visits
happening.alumniVisit.body: A retired wrestler from the stable drops by with snacks to watch practice.
happening.alumniVisit.welcome: Ask him to coach a bit
happening.alumniVisit.welcome.desc: Small training gains for everyone and a little prestige.
happening.quarrel.title: A quarrel
happening.quarrel.body: {name} and a junior are arguing over chanko duty.
happening.quarrel.letThem.desc: {name} trains a bit better, but may get hurt.
happening.veteranDoubt.title: A veteran’s doubts
happening.veteranDoubt.body: {name} mutters that it might be time to retire.
happening.veteranDoubt.encourage.desc: He trains harder. A little tired.
happening.veteranDoubt.respect.desc: He will likely ask to retire.
happening.leakyRoof.title: Leaky roof
happening.leakyRoof.body: After heavy rain, the practice room ceiling is leaking.
happening.leakyRoof.patch.desc: Cheap if it holds. If not, another ¥1M to fix it properly.
happening.leakyRoof.patch.hit: It leaked again in the next rain.
happening.managerQuits.title: Manager wants out
happening.managerQuits.body: The stable manager asks for better pay or he’ll leave.
happening.managerQuits.letGo.desc: Chores fall to the wrestlers. A little prestige lost.
happening.taxAudit.title: Tax audit
happening.taxAudit.body: The tax office wants to examine the stable’s books.
happening.taxAudit.selfHandle.desc: It may go fine. If not, ¥1.5M in back taxes.
happening.taxAudit.selfHandle.hit: Some expenses were disallowed. You paid back taxes.
happening.lodging.title: Tournament lodging
happening.lodging.body: It’s time to choose lodging for the regional tournament.
happening.lodging.temple.desc: Room to train. Slightly better gains.
happening.nutritionist.title: A nutritionist
happening.nutritionist.body: A sports nutritionist offers to review the chanko menu.
happening.nutritionist.hire.desc: Less fatigue and slightly better training for everyone.
happening.chiropractor.title: A chiropractor
happening.chiropractor.body: A chiropractor says he can cure any fatigue.
happening.chiropractor.try.desc: If it works, everyone feels fresher.
happening.chiropractor.try.hit: Everyone seems lighter on their feet.
happening.chiropractor.try.miss: Maybe it was all in their heads.
happening.ichimonMeeting.title: Ichimon meeting
happening.ichimonMeeting.body: An invitation to the ichimon elders’ meeting has arrived.
happening.ichimonMeeting.attend.desc: Fee from your savings. A little prestige.
happening.associationDuty.title: Association duty
happening.associationDuty.body: The Association has assigned you judging duty during the tournament.
happening.associationDuty.accept.desc: Prestige up. Less time to watch practice.
happening.hospitalVisit.title: Hospital visit
happening.hospitalVisit.body: A children’s hospital asks for a visit from your sekitori.
happening.disasterRelief.title: Disaster relief
happening.disasterRelief.body: A town hit by an earthquake needs help serving hot meals.
happening.disasterRelief.go: Go with the wrestlers to serve chanko
happening.overseasEvent.title: Overseas exhibition
happening.overseasEvent.body: The Association asks if your sekitori can join an overseas exhibition.
happening.newYearVisit.title: New Year
happening.newYearVisit.shrine.desc: A little prestige and a fresh start.
happening.setsubun.title: Setsubun bean-throwing
happening.setsubun.body: A shrine invites your sekitori to throw beans at Setsubun.
happening.setsubun.go.desc: A fee and a little prestige.
happening.collegeStar.title: A college champion
happening.collegeStar.body: This year’s college champion is unsure about turning pro.
happening.collegeStar.visit.desc: If he likes you, a very talented candidate joins the list.
happening.highSchoolCoach.title: A high school coach
happening.highSchoolCoach.body: A high school sumo coach wants you to look at one of his students.
happening.overseasProspect.title: A prospect from abroad
happening.overseasProspect.body: A wrestler from overseas wrote that he wants to do sumo (one foreign-born wrestler per stable).
happening.overseasProspect.meet.desc: A foreign-born candidate joins the list.
happening.surgery.title: Surgery?
happening.surgery.body: The doctor says surgery would make {name}’s injury less likely to recur.
happening.surgery.operate.desc: One more tournament out, but less injury-prone afterwards.
staff.title: Staff and chanko
staff.note: Wakaimonogashira and sewanin are Association staff, hired from retired juryo and makushita wrestlers on their stablemaster’s recommendation (the Association pays them). Choose one of each from your former wrestlers. Skill depends on their highest rank.
staff.wakaimonogashira.name: Wakaimonogashira
staff.wakaimonogashira.desc: Supervises young wrestlers. Makushita and below train better.
staff.sewanin.name: Sewanin
staff.sewanin.desc: Handles equipment and chores. Faster recovery, fewer injuries.
diet.title: Chanko policy
diet.standard.name: Standard
diet.hearty.name: Hearty
diet.hearty.desc: Wrestlers bulk up faster, but knees and backs suffer.
diet.balanced.name: Balanced
diet.frugal.name: Frugal
diet.frugal.desc: Cheaper, but wrestlers don’t grow and stay tired.
highlight.promotion.sekitori.title: Promoted to Juryo!
highlight.promotion.sekitori.body: {name} has been promoted to juryo and is now a sekitori. From now on he draws a salary, gets attendants, wears a silk belt and can tie the ginkgo-leaf topknot.
highlight.promotion.makuuchi.title: Makuuchi debut!
highlight.promotion.makuuchi.body: {name} has reached makuuchi, ranked {rank} next tournament. He will enter the ring ceremony in an apron from his supporters.
highlight.promotion.O.title: Promoted to Ozeki!
highlight.promotion.O.body: The board has approved {name}’s promotion to ozeki. Envoys from the Association come to the stable to deliver the news.
highlight.promotion.Y.title: Promoted to Yokozuna!
highlight.promotion.Y.body: On the recommendation of the Yokozuna Deliberation Council, {name} has been promoted to yokozuna. Envoys from the Association come to the stable to deliver the news.
highlight.yusho.title: {division} champion!
highlight.yusho.body: {name} won the title with {wins} wins and {losses} losses.
highlight.yusho.makuuchi: {name} won the makuuchi title with {wins} wins and {losses} losses. He holds the Emperor’s Cup and rides in the victory parade. The stable is preparing a celebration.
highlight.sansho.title: Special prize
highlight.sansho.body: {name} received the {prizes}. Each prize is worth ¥3M.
highlight.ceremony.lead: Choose the words of acceptance. He will put his resolve as {rank} into a four-character idiom.
highlight.ceremony.kojo: "I humbly accept. So as not to shame the name of {rank}, I will devote myself to sumo in the spirit of {word}."
dohyoiri.unryu.name: Unryu style
dohyoiri.unryu.desc: As he rises, the right arm extends and the left hand rests near his side. The rope has a single loop. Said to balance attack and defense.
dohyoiri.shiranui.name: Shiranui style
dohyoiri.shiranui.desc: As he rises, both arms spread wide. The rope has two loops. Said to be the attacking style.
journal.kojoDohyoiri: {shikona}’s yokozuna promotion ceremony. Idiom: "{word}". Ring entry: {dohyoiri}.
newGame.artCaption: Train your wrestlers. Build a home. Leave a legacy.
newGame.styleHelp: Your former specialty helps pupils of the same style grow.
bout.fusen: {loser} is absent, so {winner} wins by default.
traits.unknown: Not known yet (becomes clear after a few tournaments)
trait.diligent.name: Diligent
trait.lazy.name: Lazy
trait.bigStage.name: Big-stage
trait.practiceChamp.name: Practice champion
trait.practiceChamp.desc: Strong in practice, stiff in tournaments
trait.tough.name: Tough
trait.fragileBody.name: Injury-prone
trait.glutton.name: Big eater
trait.popular.name: Crowd favorite
trait.popular.desc: Draws sponsor banners in makuuchi; boosts stable prestige as a sekitori
trait.sensitive.name: Sensitive
trait.sensitive.desc: More likely to want to quit before reaching sekitori
trait.studious.name: Studious
trait.calm.name: Calm
trait.calm.desc: Steady form from tournament to tournament
rival.title: Rival stable
rival.note: A stable of another ichimon, run by a master of your generation, with banzuke strength close to yours. Beating them in sekitori bouts raises your prestige. You may compete for promising recruits; answer late and they sign there. After 3 years, if another stable becomes a closer match on the banzuke, your rival changes. Strength is the sum of rank points (yokozuna 10, ozeki 7, sanyaku 5, makuuchi 3, juryo 2, a little below).
journal.rival.new: You start to see {stable} stable, run by a contemporary, as your rival.
journal.rival.yusho: Rival {stable} stable’s {shikona} wins the makuuchi title.
journal.rival.O: Rival {stable} stable’s {shikona} is promoted to ozeki.
happening.rivalDemegeiko.title: A rival’s invitation
happening.rivalDemegeiko.body: Your rival, the master of {rival} stable, invites your wrestlers to train together.
happening.rivalDemegeiko.send.desc: Big gains and some prestige, but very tiring and risky
happening.rivalTaunt.title: Rival’s remark
happening.rivalTaunt.body: A sports paper quotes the master of {rival} stable: "I can’t see us losing to the young stables."
happening.rivalTaunt.fireUp.desc: Everyone trains harder. A little tiring
happening.rivalTaunt.laugh.desc: Your composure earns a little prestige
election.title: Board election
election.recommended: The biennial board election follows this tournament. Your ichimon has nominated you for {seat}.
election.notRecommended: The biennial board election follows this tournament. Your ichimon did not nominate you. Running anyway forces a vote (about {percent}% chance to win).
election.note: With your ichimon’s backing it is settled without a vote. Running without it raises prestige if you win and costs prestige if you lose. Directors earn more and gain prestige, but without a coach in the stable they have less time for practice.
board.title: The board
board.none: No election yet (every two years, after the January tournament).
board.note: Offices rise from elder to chief, committee member and senior committee member; directors are elected and the chairman is chosen from them.
journal.election.electedRebel: Ran without the ichimon’s backing and was elected {office}.
journal.election.lostRebel: Ran without the ichimon’s backing and lost.
koenkai.title: Supporters’ club
koenkai.party.none.desc: No cost, but membership shrinks and patrons cool off.
koenkai.party.small.desc: A modest celebration at the stable. Normal membership growth.
koenkai.party.grand.desc: A grand hotel party. Membership grows, patrons warm up and prestige rises.
koenkai.noPatrons: No patrons right now. They come as you produce sekitori and gain prestige.
koenkai.note: Member dues and patrons’ gifts reach the stable account each tournament. Patrons are pleased when their favorite wins or is promoted; left alone they slowly cool off (visits are paid from your savings). All amounts are estimates.
patron.kind.brewery: The head of the {surname} sake brewery
scout.title: Go scouting
scout.note: The master goes out to meet prospects. Anyone you meet joins the candidate list (you still decide whether to accept). Once per tournament, paid from the stable account (estimates).
scout.doneNote: You already went this tournament. You can go again next time.
scout.noMoney: Not enough in the stable account
scout.foreignLimit: Only one foreign-born wrestler per stable
scout.juniorHighMeet.name: National junior high tournament
scout.juniorHighMeet.desc: The August national meet. Meet 1–3 fifteen-year-olds with lots of room to grow
scout.interHigh.name: High school nationals
scout.interHigh.desc: The August high school championships. Meet 1–2 experienced 18-year-olds
scout.collegeMeet.name: National college championships
scout.collegeMeet.desc: The November college championships. Meet 1–2 ready-made 22-year-olds
scout.countryside.name: Follow up local rumors
scout.countryside.desc: Meet 0–2 athletes from other sports. You may come back empty-handed
scout.overseas.name: Go abroad
scout.overseas.desc: Meet one talented young athlete from abroad. Expensive
journal.scoutNone: Went to {trip} but found no one promising.
guide.title: Getting started
guide.lead: Start here. Steps are checked off as you go.
guide.step.policy: Choose each wrestler’s training (push, belt, technique, body, rest)
guide.step.basho: Press “To the tournament” to play the 15 days
guide.step.bout: In the results, press a ○/● mark to watch the bout
guide.step.ledger: Open the Ledger tab to see the money
guide.tip.stable: Stable: each pre-basho week, choose one command. Tap a wrestler to talk. When ready, press “To the tournament” below.
guide.tip.banzuke: Rankings: every wrestler’s rank. Yours are marked ◆. Switch divisions at the top.
guide.tip.ledger: Ledger: last tournament’s money. Manage supporters, staff, chanko and facilities here. Deficits come out of your savings.
guide.tip.lineage: Lineage: past masters and the family tree. Coaches you raise become heirs or open branch stables.
guide.tip.association: Association: your rival, the board, the five ichimon and free elder names.
guide.tip.journal: Journal: the stable’s history. Export and import saves here too.
highlight.danpatsu.title: Hair-Cutting Ceremony
highlight.danpatsu.kokugikan: At the Kokugikan, the retirement ceremony for {name} (highest rank {rank}). After bouts and sumo songs, about {hasami} people stepped onto the ring one by one to snip his topknot.
highlight.danpatsu.hotel: In a hotel banquet hall, the hair-cutting ceremony for {name} (highest rank {rank}). About {hasami} people took a snip of his topknot.
highlight.danpatsu.cut: Finally, his master {master} made the last cut, and the topknot fell.
highlight.danpatsu.afterOyakata: From now on he stays as an elder, raising the next wrestlers.
highlight.danpatsu.afterLeave: {name} heads into a second life without a topknot.
journal.danpatsu.kokugikan: Retirement ceremony for {shikona} at the Kokugikan. About {hasami} people took a snip.
journal.danpatsu.hotel: Hair-cutting ceremony for {shikona}. About {hasami} people took a snip.
fame.title: Hall of Fame ({count})
fame.note: Former wrestlers who reached yokozuna or ozeki, won a top-division title, or took 5+ special prizes. Tap for details.
fame.empty: No one yet. When a yokozuna, ozeki or top-division champion retires, his name stays here.
records.title: Stable Records
records.empty: No pupil has appeared on the banzuke yet.
records.note: Current pupils are marked "Active". When one breaks a record, you hear about it after the tournament.
highlight.record.title: Stable Record
highlight.record.body: {name} set a new stable record for {record}: {value} (previously {prevName}, {prevValue}).
race.title: Top-Division Title Race
race.decidedPlayoff: Still level after the final day, it went to a playoff.
race.after14: After Day 14, these wrestlers were still in the title race.
journal.rival.switch: Now neck and neck on the banzuke, the {stable} stable becomes your new rival (moving on from {from}).
rikishi.oldInjuryDesc: Even after healing, he gets hurt more easily (often in the same place).
treatment.label: Treatment
treatment.note: Injured {part} (out {total} tournament(s)). Surgery means one more tournament out but rarely leaves an old injury. Rest gets him back sooner but often leaves one. If you don't answer, he rests.
journal.injury.chronic: {shikona}'s {part} healed, but it remains an old injury.
mid.title: After {day}
mid.lead: The first eight days are over. Before the second half (from day 9), choose how each wrestler fights and whether to send in those sitting out.
mid.note: Sending him back keeps the missed days as losses, but he can win back bouts in the remaining days. Fighting hurt lowers his condition, makes new injuries likelier, and can slow or worsen his recovery.
report.reentered: Returned in the second half: {names} (fighting hurt may slow recovery)
scene.keikoba: The stable's practice room: the ring, a teppo pole and the master's raised seat
scene.exterior: The stable from outside: the main house and the wrestlers' dormitory
scene.jungyo: A regional tour venue: an outdoor ring under a hanging roof, with red-and-white curtains and a tent
voice.injured.0: Sorry, Master… I'll heal fast and get back on the ring.
voice.injured.1: Sitting still is the hardest part.
voice.injured.2: They tell me not to rush. I'm rushing anyway.
voice.newcomer.0: Pleased to meet you! I'll do anything!
voice.newcomer.1: I don't know left from right yet. But the chanko is great.
voice.tired.1: Could I rest, just a little?
voice.tired.2: I can't lift my legs. My shiko isn't shiko anymore.
voice.hard.0: It's brutal. But I think I'm getting stronger.
voice.hard.1: Hard practice? Bring it on. …Tomorrow too, right?
voice.great.0: My body moved well last tournament. I'll keep it going!
voice.great.1: I can't wait for the new banzuke. Thank you, Master.
voice.kachikoshi.0: I'm relieved I got my winning record.
voice.kachikoshi.1: I'm starting to hold my own against the men above me.
voice.kachikoshi.2: Next time I'll line up more wins.
voice.makekoshi.0: A losing record stings. I'll answer in practice.
voice.makekoshi.1: I keep asking myself what I'm missing.
voice.makekoshi.2: I hesitated at the charge. Never again.
voice.nearSekitori.0: So close to sekitori. I dream of the white mawashi.
voice.nearSekitori.1: This is the moment that counts. I know.
voice.sekitori.0: I want my attendants to share the good times.
voice.sekitori.1: I'll wrestle in a way worthy of a sekitori.
voice.sekitori.2: I'm finally learning the weight of a prize envelope.
voice.veteran.0: The body is honest, but my sumo can still grow.
voice.veteran.1: I have to show the young ones my back.
voice.sensitive.0: Master… am I cut out for this?
voice.oshi.0: Forward, forward. That's all I think about.
voice.oshi.1: A thousand teppo strikes, coming up.
voice.yotsu.0: Once I have the belt, I won't lose.
voice.waza.0: Using the other man's strength is the fun of sumo.
voice.waza.1: I'm drilling suriashi into my body.
voice.body.0: Eat, sleep, shiko. I'm building my body.
voice.rest.1: My body is starting to feel light again.
talk.title: Talk to {name}
talk.hint: Tap a wrestler in the scene to talk and set his training.
intensity.label: Workload
intensity.desc.light: Smaller gains, but less fatigue and fewer injuries.
intensity.desc.hard: Bigger gains, but fatigue builds and injuries are likelier. A wrestler at the wall gains talent.
mid.stanceNote: "Go all out" lifts second-half form but raises injury risk and leaves fatigue after the tournament. "Play it safe" lowers form but makes injuries less likely.
stance.desc.push: Better form, but more injuries and lingering fatigue.
report.training.name: Wrestler
bigBout.title: Everything on one bout
bigBout.stakes: {name} steps up on {day} at {wins}–{losses}. Win for a winning record, lose for a losing one. The opponent is {opponent} ({stable}).
bigBout.lost: {opponent} wins by {kimarite}. {name} finishes {wins}–{losses}: a losing record.
goals.title: The stable's path
goals.allDone: Every milestone is behind you. Now: how long can this lineage last?
goals.sandanme.name: Reach sandanme
goals.sandanme.hint: Winning records carry a wrestler out of jonokuchi and jonidan. Start by setting each wrestler's training policy.
goals.makushita.name: Reach makushita
goals.makushita.hint: Sandanme is a deep division. Grow each wrestler's style and rest him when fatigue builds.
goals.sekitori.name: Produce your first sekitori (juryo)
goals.sekitori.hint: Winning records inside makushita 15 bring juryo into view. A sekitori means a white mawashi, banners and more support money.
goals.makuuchi.name: Produce a makuuchi wrestler
goals.makuuchi.hint: Double-digit wins in juryo bring promotion close. A stronger supporters' club pays for treatment and facilities.
goals.sanyaku.name: Produce a sanyaku wrestler
goals.sanyaku.hint: A winning record in upper maegashira earns sanyaku. He will face every yokozuna and ozeki, so the mid-basho stance matters.
goals.sekitori3.name: Raise three sekitori
goals.sekitori3.hint: Find talented recruits and improve the practice room and dormitory to raise the next sekitori.
goals.yusho.name: Win the makuuchi title
goals.yusho.hint: Stay in the race until the final day, then it is one big bout. Push hard in training, or avoid injury: your call.
goals.ozeki.name: Produce an ozeki
goals.ozeki.hint: About 33 wins over three tournaments in sanyaku. Keep him healthy and winning.
goals.yokozuna.name: Produce a yokozuna
goals.yokozuna.hint: Back-to-back titles as ozeki, or the equivalent. The pride of the stable.
goals.succession.name: Hand the stable to the next generation
goals.succession.hint: Raise a successor who holds elder stock before the master retires. Long-serving sekitori become candidates.
ticker.legend: ○ win, ● loss, □ win by default, ■ loss by default, · no bout that day. Makushita and below fight seven bouts.
prep.title: Before the tournament
prep.done: Training is done. On to the tournament.
prep.logAria: What you did before this tournament
prep.desc.coach: Coach one wrestler. His focus grows. A wrestler at the wall gains talent.
prep.desc.spar: Two wrestlers spar. The one facing a stronger man grows more.
prep.desc.degeiko: Train at another stable. Everyone healthy grows a little.
prep.desc.visit: Meet one patron. Your relationship improves.
prep.desc.scout: Go looking for recruits. More wrestlers fill the stable account. Once per basho.
target.label: Goal
target.danger: A losing record drops him to {to}
prep.desc.mune: Send one to train with sekitori. Big gains and breaks walls, but exhausting.
delegate.title: Delegated: {n} tournament(s)
delegate.stop.gameOver: The stable can no longer continue.
delegate.stop.injury: A wrestler was injured. Choose his treatment.
delegate.stop.promotion: A promotion to sekitori or higher!
delegate.stop.money: Money is running out. Check the ledger.
rewards.title: Effects on the stable
rewards.none: Nothing that moved the stable much.
outlook.title: Outlook
prep.wallDesc: Has hit the wall of his talent. Hard training raises the talent itself.
tactic.title: Game plan for the big bout
tactic.lead: A winning record is on the line. Read his opponent's style and set the tachiai plan.
tactic.desc.atari: Charge head-first and push. Strong against technicians.
tactic.desc.sashi: Get inside and hold. Strong against pushers.
tactic.desc.henka: Sidestep at the tachiai. Strong against belt fighters, bad if read. Even a win costs prestige and patron goodwill.
prep.confirm.title: Go with this?
prep.confirm.fill: Spend the remaining {n} week(s) as usual
event.title: Event
guide.tip.deshi: Wrestlers: tap one to change his training focus and workload.
pay.fromSavings: {yen} not covered by the stable account comes from your savings
tide.yokozuna.name: Another stable's yokozuna offers his chest
tide.yokozuna.desc: Borrowing a chest grows more than usual
tide.rengo.name: Joint ichimon practice
tide.rengo.desc: Away practice is free and grows more
tide.spirit.name: The deshi are fired up
tide.spirit.desc: Sparring grows more, with fewer injuries
tide.cool.name: A crisp, clear week
tide.cool.desc: Coaching grows more and tires less
tide.festival.name: Local festival
tide.rumor.name: Word of a promising kid
tide.rumor.desc: Scouting meets more kids, with more talent
tide.seitai.name: A bodyworker visits
tide.rain.name: Long rains
tide.harsh.name: Rough mood in the practice ring
tide.harsh.desc: Practice tires more, with more injuries
tide.cold.name: A cold is going around
tide.cold.desc: Practice grows less, and rest clears less fatigue
pledge.title: A pledge to the supporters
pledge.lead: New year. Pledge something to the supporters' club and get an advance now. Break it and you pay it back.
pledge.kachikoshi.name: Keep winning records ({share}% or more)
pledge.division.name: Lift the stable's top deshi a division
pledge.sekitori.name: Produce a new sekitori
pledge.terms: Advance {advance}. Kept: prestige +{prestige} / broken: repay, prestige −{fail}, members −{members}%
journal.pledge.broken: Broke the pledge “{pledge}” and repaid the advance.
glossary.title: Sumo notebook
glossary.note: Words you meet while running the stable collect here.
glossary.term.asageiko.name: Morning practice
glossary.term.asageiko.desc: Up at 5–6, practice before any breakfast. The lowest ranks take the ring first; sekitori come last.
glossary.term.chanko.name: Chanko
glossary.term.chanko.desc: The wrestlers' meal. Lunch after practice is the first meal of the day; the master and sekitori eat first, juniors serve, then eat.
glossary.term.chankoban.name: Chanko duty
glossary.term.chankoban.desc: The cooking rota, shared by makushita and below. Many stables excuse upper makushita (around the top 15) and promising deshi.
glossary.term.shiko.name: Shiko
glossary.term.shiko.desc: The basic leg-raise and stamp. Builds legs and core; done every day.
glossary.term.teppo.name: Teppo
glossary.term.teppo.desc: Thrusting a post with alternating hands. Drills the shape of the push and links arms to hips.
glossary.term.moshiai.name: Moshiai
glossary.term.moshiai.desc: The winner stays in the ring and names the next opponent. Two evenly matched wrestlers going again and again is sanban-geiko.
glossary.term.butsukari.name: Butsukari
glossary.term.butsukari.desc: Charge into the receiver's chest and drive him to the edge, then roll to break the fall. The hardest drill.
glossary.term.tsukebito.name: Tsukebito
glossary.term.tsukebito.desc: Makushita and below who attend a sekitori: 2–3 for juryo, 8–10 for a yokozuna. They carry his trunk, tie his belt, wash his back.
glossary.term.okamisan.name: Okamisan
glossary.term.okamisan.desc: The master's wife. Keeps the books, deals with supporters, and looks after the deshi.
glossary.term.unten.name: No driving
glossary.term.unten.desc: Active wrestlers may not drive cars or bikes (an Association rule). They can hold a licence, but may drive only after retiring.
glossary.term.kensa.name: Recruit exam
glossary.term.kensa.desc: The entry exam: 167 cm and 67 kg, or else an athletic test. There is a medical check too.
glossary.term.maezumo.name: Maezumo
glossary.term.maezumo.desc: Bouts before one's name is on the banzuke. Today a single bout is enough to be promoted, win or lose.
glossary.term.shusse.name: Shinjo shusse hiro
glossary.term.shusse.desc: The ring-side debut of new recruits. Having no kesho-mawashi yet, they wear ones borrowed from the master or seniors.
glossary.term.kyoshujo.name: Sumo school
glossary.term.kyoshujo.desc: The recruits' school inside the Kokugikan. Six months of basics plus sumo history, calligraphy and sumo songs.
glossary.term.shikona.name: Shikona
glossary.term.shikona.desc: A wrestler's ring name, often carrying one character of the master's.
glossary.term.banzuke.name: Banzuke
glossary.term.banzuke.desc: The ranking sheet, released about two weeks before the first day.
glossary.term.sekitori.name: Sekitori
glossary.term.sekitori.desc: Juryo and above: a monthly salary, a private room, attendants. The gap to makushita is the biggest in sumo.
glossary.term.oicho.name: Oicho-mage
glossary.term.oicho.desc: The ginkgo-leaf topknot sekitori wear in bouts. Lower ranks wear the plain chonmage.
glossary.term.kachikoshi.name: Kachi-koshi
glossary.term.kachikoshi.desc: More wins than losses: 8 for sekitori, 4 below. The usual mark for moving up.
glossary.term.hensei.name: Banzuke meeting
glossary.term.hensei.desc: Held within three days of a tournament to set the next banzuke and decide ozeki, yokozuna and juryo promotions.
glossary.term.kadoban.name: Kadoban
glossary.term.kadoban.desc: A tournament an ozeki must not lose; two losing records in a row and he drops.
glossary.term.tsuna.name: Yokozuna
glossary.term.tsuna.desc: The top rank, earned by two straight titles as ozeki or the equivalent. He never drops; when results fail, he retires.
glossary.term.mochikyukin.name: Mochikyukin
glossary.term.mochikyukin.desc: Points earned by winning records and gold stars; x4000 is paid every tournament. They never go down.
glossary.term.mina.name: Dress by rank
glossary.term.mina.desc: Rank decides dress: yukata and geta to jonidan, setta and haori at sandanme, coat and tabi at makushita, crested kimono at juryo.
glossary.term.kesho.name: Kesho-mawashi
glossary.term.kesho.desc: The embroidered apron sekitori wear for the ring entrance. Usually a gift from supporters or the hometown; several million yen.
glossary.term.shimekomi.name: Shimekomi
glossary.term.shimekomi.desc: The silk belt sekitori fight in. Their practice belts are white; lower ranks wear black.
glossary.term.akeni.name: Akeni
glossary.term.akeni.desc: The woven trunk a sekitori brings to the arena, holding his aprons and belt. By custom, a gift from his intake-mates.
glossary.term.dohyomatsuri.name: Dohyo-matsuri
glossary.term.dohyomatsuri.desc: The ring-blessing the day before a tournament, welcoming the gods; on the last day they are sent off.
glossary.term.nakabi.name: Nakabi
glossary.term.nakabi.desc: Day 8 of 15: the turn from the first half to the second.
glossary.term.senshuraku.name: Senshuraku
glossary.term.senshuraku.desc: The final day: the title is decided and prizes awarded.
glossary.term.kensho.name: Kensho
glossary.term.kensho.desc: Sponsors' prize money on a bout: 70,000 yen a banner, 60,000 to the winner (10,000 in the ring, 50,000 to his account).
glossary.term.sansho.name: Sansho
glossary.term.sansho.desc: The three special prizes for makuuchi — outstanding performance, fighting spirit, technique — for standouts at sekiwake or below (a winning record is the usual bar, though no written rule requires it).
glossary.term.kinboshi.name: Kinboshi (gold star)
glossary.term.kinboshi.desc: A maegashira beating a yokozuna. It raises the wrestler's mochikyukin by 10 yen, increasing his bonus every tournament until retirement.
glossary.term.jungyo.name: Jungyo
glossary.term.jungyo.desc: Regional tours between tournaments: open practice, bouts with children, comic shokkiri, hair-dressing shows and handshakes.
glossary.term.shokkiri.name: Shokkiri
glossary.term.shokkiri.desc: Comic sumo on tour, acting out the forbidden moves.
glossary.term.toshiyori.name: Toshiyori name
glossary.term.toshiyori.desc: The 105 elder names that let a retired wrestler stay as a stablemaster; none free, no place.
glossary.term.ichimon.name: Ichimon
glossary.term.ichimon.desc: A group of linked stables. Branches stay in the parent's ichimon, which fields candidates in board elections.
glossary.term.heyatsuki.name: Heya-tsuki
glossary.term.heyatsuki.desc: An elder attached to a stable without running it. He coaches, and may later branch out.
glossary.term.rijisen.name: Board election
glossary.term.rijisen.desc: Every two years. Each ichimon puts up candidates; most seats are settled without a vote.
glossary.term.dentatsu.name: Promotion ceremony
glossary.term.dentatsu.desc: Envoys announce an ozeki or yokozuna promotion; the wrestler answers with a vow, often a four-character idiom.
glossary.term.danpatsu.name: Danpatsu-shiki
glossary.term.danpatsu.desc: The retirement haircut. Many take a snip; the master makes the final cut.
glossary.term.tanimachi.name: Tanimachi
glossary.term.tanimachi.desc: A patron of a wrestler or stable, helping with gifts and dinners.
glossary.term.boryoku.name: Anti-violence pledge
glossary.term.boryoku.desc: The Association's 2018 declaration: all violence banned, and a master's violence punished up to demotion or closing the stable.
highlight.sekitori.room: From the big room to a private room
highlight.sekitori.pay: A monthly salary of {yen} (below, only a per-tournament allowance)
highlight.sekitori.hair: The oicho-mage in bouts; a white practice belt and a silk shimekomi
highlight.sekitori.dress: Crested kimono with hakama, and white tabi
highlight.sekitori.akeniNone: No intake-mates are left in the ring; the master provided the akeni
kesho.title: The kesho-mawashi
kesho.lead: What will {name} wear for the ring entrance?
kesho.patron.name: Ask our patron {surname}
kesho.patron.desc: No cost. He becomes {surname}'s favourite and the bond grows
kesho.stable.name: Have the stable make one ({yen})
kesho.stable.desc: Prestige rises and the supporters' club grows a little
kesho.borrowed.name: Borrow the master's for now
journal.akeni: New juryo {shikona} received an akeni from {doki} intake-mates.
journal.akeniNone: The master provided new juryo {shikona}'s akeni.
journal.kesho.stable: The stable had a kesho-mawashi made for {shikona}.
journal.kesho.borrowed: {shikona} borrows the master's kesho-mawashi for now.
role.title: Role in the stable
role.desc.tsukebito: Attends {name}. Sparring with a sekitori helps him grow a little, but the chores tire him
role.desc.chankoban: Chanko duty, shared by {n}. Growth dips a little and he tires
role.desc.upper: Top 15 in makushita, so off chanko duty
role.desc.noCook: No one is on chanko duty. Everyone recovers more slowly
highlight.shusse.title: Shinjo shusse hiro
highlight.shusse.body: Their maezumo done, {names} stepped into the ring in a kesho-mawashi borrowed from {lender} and were announced by name. Next tournament, they appear on the banzuke in jonokuchi.
dress.title: Dress
dress.level.0: Yukata, bare feet in geta, black practice belt
dress.level.1: Setta sandals and a haori jacket allowed
dress.level.2: Coat, scarf, hakata obi and tabi allowed
dress.level.3: Crested kimono with hakama, white tabi, oicho-mage, white practice belt, silk shimekomi, kesho-mawashi
dress.level.4: May have yukata dyed with his shikona
happening.drivingLicense.title: A driving licence
happening.drivingLicense.body: {name} wants to get a licence and buy a car. Active wrestlers are not allowed to drive.
happening.drivingLicense.licenseOnly: Let him get the licence only
happening.drivingLicense.licenseOnly.des: Driving waits for retirement. It gives him something to look forward to
happening.drivingLicense.lookAway.desc: If he drives and it comes out, prestige and money suffer
happening.drivingLicense.lookAway.hit: {name} was photographed driving; the Association gave a stern warning.
happening.violenceRumor.title: A senior's hand
happening.violenceRumor.body: Word reaches you that a senior struck a junior. The Association declared an end to violence in 2018.
happening.violenceRumor.report.desc: Prestige dips a little, but it goes no further
happening.violenceRumor.hush.desc: Nothing if it stays inside; heavy penalties if it gets out
happening.violenceRumor.hush.hit: A weekly ran the story and the Association imposed penalties.
happening.violenceRumor.decline.desc: The juniors are cowed and a little tired
happening.lateNight.title: Late nights
happening.lateNight.body: {name} keeps his attendants out drinking late. They are unsteady at morning practice.
happening.lateNight.decline: Let it go as sekitori business
happening.curfew.title: Missed curfew
happening.curfew.extraChores.desc: {name} tires, but tightens up and practises harder
happening.curfew.decline.desc: If it keeps happening, the stable's name may suffer
happening.curfew.decline.hit: Neighbours complained, and the stable's reputation slipped.
happening.calligraphy.title: Calligraphy class
happening.calligraphy.body: At the sumo school, the teacher praised {name}'s brushwork.
happening.calligraphy.frame.desc: Visitors notice; prestige rises a little
happening.calligraphy.praise.desc: {name} is spurred on and grows more next practice
happening.jinku.title: Sumo jinku
happening.jinku.body: {name}, who learned sumo jinku songs at the school, wants to sing at the supporters' banquet.
happening.jinku.sing.desc: A gift and a little prestige. {name} tires a little
happening.tsukebitoCare.title: A thoughtful attendant
happening.tsukebitoCare.body: Attendant {name}'s care has become the talk of the sekitori.
happening.tsukebitoCare.praise: Praise him in front of everyone
happening.tsukebitoCare.praise.desc: {name} is spurred on and grows more next practice; tires a little
happening.shitakuPhone.title: A phone in the dressing room
happening.shitakuPhone.body: {name} was about to take a phone into the dressing room, where phones are banned.
happening.shitakuPhone.decline.desc: If he is caught, the stable's name suffers
happening.shitakuPhone.decline.hit: An official caught him mid-tournament and the stable was named.
happening.shitakuPhone.decline.miss: He has not done it again.
living.alone.desc: Lives outside the stable and comes in to practise. Recovers better, but the master sees less of him
living.married.desc: Married and living outside the stable. Rests at home and recovers well
glossary.term.kurashi.name: Where sekitori live
glossary.term.kurashi.desc: Makushita and below sleep in the stable's big room. Sekitori may marry or move out and live alone.
journal.living.alone: {shikona} moved out of the stable to live alone.
journal.living.back: {shikona}, no longer a sekitori, moved back into the big room.
happening.marriage.title: Wedding news
happening.marriage.body: {name} came to say there is someone he wants to marry.
happening.marriage.bless.desc: A gift from your savings. Prestige rises a little and {name} is spurred on. He will live outside the stable
happening.marriage.decline: Ask him to wait a while
happening.moveOut.title: Moving out
happening.moveOut.body: {name} wants to leave the stable and live on his own, as sekitori may.
happening.moveOut.allow.desc: He comes in to practise. Recovers better, grows a little less
happening.moveOut.decline.desc: {name} is a little unhappy and tired
soken.line: Before this tournament, {names} will attend the Yokozuna Council's open practice (a little growth, some fatigue)
highlight.yokozuna.tsuna: Tsuna-uchi: stable and ichimon wrestlers gather to twist a new rope
highlight.yokozuna.escortIchimon: a makuuchi wrestler from the ichimon
highlight.yokozuna.yumitoriNone: Bow ceremony: no lower-rankers in the stable, so an ichimon wrestler performs it
highlight.shusse.teuchi: On the final day they clapped in the shusse teuchi-shiki and tossed the referee to send off the gods.
role.desc.yumitori: From yokozuna {name}'s stable, he performs the bow ceremony after the last bout each day
glossary.term.soken.name: Soken
glossary.term.soken.desc: Before each Tokyo tournament (January, May, September), the Yokozuna Council watches sekitori practise. Mid-maegashira and up are expected. The May one is open to the public.
glossary.term.yumitori.name: Yumitori-shiki
glossary.term.yumitori.desc: The bow ceremony after the last bout of each day, performed by a makushita-or-lower wrestler, often from the yokozuna's stable or ichimon.
glossary.term.tsuyuharai.name: Tsuyuharai and tachimochi
glossary.term.tsuyuharai.desc: The two makuuchi wrestlers who escort a yokozuna's ring entrance: the dew-sweeper in front, the sword-bearer behind. From his stable, or else his ichimon.
glossary.term.tsunauchi.name: Tsuna-uchi
glossary.term.tsunauchi.desc: Stable and ichimon wrestlers gather to twist the yokozuna's rope — for a new yokozuna, and again before each Tokyo tournament.
glossary.term.kamiokuri.name: Teuchi-shiki and kami-okuri
glossary.term.kamiokuri.desc: After the final day's prizes, that tournament's new recruits clap together in the ring and toss the referee to send off the gods.
glossary.term.shitakubeya.name: Shitaku-beya
glossary.term.shitakubeya.desc: The dressing rooms, east and west, where wrestlers put on belts and warm up. Phones are not allowed.
glossary.term.uragata.name: Gyoji, yobidashi, tokoyama
glossary.term.uragata.desc: Referees, ring announcers who also tend the ring, and hairdressers. All belong to stables.
happening.jungyoShokkiri.title: Shokkiri on tour
happening.jungyoShokkiri.body: On tour, {name} was asked to perform shokkiri, comic sumo acting out the forbidden moves.
happening.jungyoShokkiri.perform.desc: The crowd roars; prestige rises a little. {name} tires a little
happening.jungyoChibikko.title: Children's sumo
happening.jungyoChibikko.body: At the tour venue, {name} will let local children charge into his chest.
happening.jungyoChibikko.lend.desc: Prestige rises a little. A child may want to join
happening.jungyoChibikko.lend.hit: A junior-high boy came with his parents: “I want to be like him.”
happening.jungyoHandshake.title: Tour handshakes
happening.jungyoHandshake.body: The handshake line for {name} on tour stretches a long way.
happening.jungyoKamiyui.title: Hair-dressing show
happening.jungyoKamiyui.body: At the tour venue, a tokoyama will dress {name}'s oicho-mage in front of the crowd.
happening.jungyoKeiko.title: Tour morning practice
happening.jungyoKeiko.body: At morning practice on tour, another stable's yokozuna offered {name} his chest.
happening.jungyoKeiko.go.desc: Grows a lot, tires badly, risk of injury
happening.jungyoTravel.title: Tour travel
happening.jungyoTravel.body: Days of bus rides on tour have worn down the sekitori.
happening.jungyoTravel.push.desc: Prestige rises a little; the sekitori tire more
happening.jungyoTravel.decline.desc: The sekitori recover; prestige dips a little

uragata.tokoyama.name: Tokoyama
uragata.tokoyama.desc: Dresses topknots. Keeps sekitori looked after, so they recover better
uragata.yobidashi.name: Yobidashi
uragata.yobidashi.desc: Calls wrestlers and tends the ring. A better practice ring means fewer injuries
uragata.gyoji.name: Gyoji
uragata.gyoji.desc: Referees bouts, and helps with paperwork and tour arrangements; prestige rises slowly

glossary.term.yusho.name: Yusho (championship)
glossary.term.yusho.desc: The wrestler with the most wins in each division. Ties are settled by a playoff on the final day. The makuuchi champion receives the Emperor's Cup.
glossary.term.zensho.name: Zensho (perfect record)
glossary.term.zensho.desc: Winning every bout of the tournament (15 for sekitori, 7 below). A title won this way is a zensho yusho.
glossary.term.nenkan.name: Most wins of the year
glossary.term.nenkan.desc: The wrestler with the most wins across the year's six tournaments, kept as a record of steady strength apart from rank and titles.
kimariteBook.title: Kimarite book
achv.kimarite20.name: Bag of tricks
achv.kimarite20.hint: Win with 20 different kimarite as a stable (excluding non-techniques)
kimarite.desc.tsukidashi: Drive the opponent out with thrusts.
kimarite.desc.oshidashi: Push the opponent out without a belt grip.
kimarite.desc.yorikiri: Close in and drive the opponent out. The most common kimarite.
kimarite.desc.yoritaoshi: Force out and topple the opponent.
kimarite.desc.abisetaoshi: Bear down with your body and topple the opponent backward.
kimarite.desc.uwatenage: Overarm throw, gripping the belt over the opponent's arm.
kimarite.desc.shitatenage: Underarm throw, gripping the belt under the opponent's arm.
kimarite.desc.kotenage: Armlock throw: trap the opponent's arm and throw without a belt grip.
kimarite.desc.sukuinage: Beltless arm throw, scooping under the armpit.
kimarite.desc.hatakikomi: Slap the charging opponent down by the shoulders or back.
kimarite.desc.hikiotoshi: Pull the opponent forward and down.
kimarite.desc.okuridashi: Push the opponent out from behind.
kimarite.desc.tsuridashi: Lift the opponent by the belt and carry him out.
kimarite.desc.isamiashi: Stepping out by yourself while pressing forward (a non-technique).
